name: Ogee curve analysis
lead: In aesthetic facial surgery, the ogee curve describes the S-shaped line running from the cheekbone (malar prominence) down into the mid-cheek hollow [1]. The word comes from geometry, where an ogee is an S-shaped curve joining a concave arc to a convex arc, and it is also used in architecture and engineering [1].

Mid-face rejuvenation in the surgical literature often aims to restore or smooth this curve [1]. Filler papers describe a smooth ogee curve, along with an oval face, pronounced cheekbones and a defined jawline, as global aesthetic goals [2][3]. On looksmax.org the curve is analyzed as a feature separating more attractive faces from average ones [4].
infobox: Hollow cheeks, midface volume, cheek fillers

paras: Geometrically, an ogee has a concave arc and a convex arc meeting at an inflection point, with end tangents roughly parallel; it appears in Gothic arches, mouldings, ship hulls, dam spillways and aircraft wing design [1]. In facial aesthetics the term borrows that shape for the cheek profile [1].

No studies found testing the ogee curve as a predictor of attractiveness. Published case reports and technique papers use it as a treatment goal: a filler paper describes injection points intended to achieve a smooth ogee curve while avoiding bulkiness [5], another discusses fillers for an Indian face with different skeletal and soft tissue proportions [2], and an amniotic allograft study addressed midface aging correction [6]. A paper on infraorbital hyaluronic acid injection technique also addresses the region [7].

A widely viewed looksmax.org thread by the user Clavicular says the ogee curve is extremely important for attractiveness in men and women, and attributes the shape to the zygomatic bones, gonions and masseter muscles [4]. The thread also covers buccal fat removal and other methods, and mentions an account of a self-performed buccal fat removal that went wrong [4]. Responses in the thread were largely positive [4].

lore.intro: The ogee curve is promoted on looksmax.org as a key feature, with the thread's author ranking it among the most important for attractiveness [4].

claims.claim: A clear ogee curve separates a "chad" from a "normie".
claims.believers: The thread's author says the curve is extremely important for attractiveness in men and women, and explains it through zygomatic projection, gonial shape and the masseter [4].
claims.experts: Surgical papers describe a smooth ogee curve as an aesthetic goal in filler and midface work [2][5], but no study found tests it as a determinant of attractiveness.

card.summary: The S-shaped line from cheekbone to cheek hollow, used as a goal in filler surgery and as a hotly promoted beauty marker online.
card.note: Appears as a treatment goal in filler papers; no study tests it as a driver of attractiveness.

quick.overview:
The ogee curve is the S-shaped contour from the cheekbone into the hollow of the mid-cheek. Surgeons talk about restoring it in midface rejuvenation.

Looksmax.org members call it a major feature for attractiveness. No study tested that claim.
quick.mechanism: Forum members tie the curve to zygomatic projection, gonial flare and masseter size. Clinicians describe adjusting it with fillers or other midface volume treatments.
quick.risks: The concept itself is descriptive. Procedures used to pursue it, such as fillers or buccal fat removal, carry their own risks; forums also contain accounts of a self-performed buccal fat removal that went wrong.
